newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht rallies late as rates hit speculators.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht rallies late as rates hit speculators.

text.p: The Thai baht rallied in late trade on Thursday as the central bank allowed banks to quote Friday for Monday delivery deals for overseas clients at high financing costs, dealers said.
The high baht rates foiled speculators, severely tightened liquidity and renewed interest in the baht, they added.

The baht strengthened to 25.300/25.340 per dollar at 1022 GMT from 25.910/25.940 early, dealers said. The Bank of Thailand fixed the mid-rate at 25.81 a dollar against 25.85 on Wednesday. "The spot market was quite calm down today with more dollar being offered in the market," said a dealer at a foreign bank.
The Bank of Thailand stressed on Thursday it would maintain high interest rates to defend against speculative attacks on the currency.

The offshore players also found it difficult to borrow funds for speculation in the baht as the central bank was earlier said to inform banks in Thailand not quote to offshore parties for tom/next activities, dealers said.
However, the central bank in the afternoon allowed banks to resume quoting tom/next to non-resident clients.
"We are allowed to resume quoting tom/next (for Friday dollar/baht deals and Monday delivery) for overseas clients but at about two baht," said one broker at a foreign bank. said.
The authorities made it clear that local banks would have to offer funds at high financing costs to discourage speculation against the baht, she added.
Most players were also wary of pushing the baht down further amid worries about another intervention by Bank of Thailand and its regional counterparts to defend the currency, dealers said.
Central banks of Thailand and Singapore on Wednesday jointly intervened in the Singapore market to stabilise the battered baht.
The Bank of Japan said on Thursday it may join hands with other Asian central banks and intervene in foreign exchange markets to help support the baht if asked to do so by Thailand.
But forward premiums were shooting up further due to a severe shortage of funds after recent buying of the dollar by speculators, dealers said.
The one-month baht/dollar swap premium jumped to 15.00/16.00 satangs per dollar late from 12.00/13.00 in early morning, dealers said.
The overnight interbank rate eased to 14.00-15.00 percent late from 18.00-20.00 percent early, dealers said.
"Most banks had done nothing today. But I heard the rate of 14.00-15.00 was being done in the market in the afternoon," said one money market dealer.
